title: The aim
text:
You are a wizard with a deck of cards. So is everyone else. Bring every opponent's life down to nothing and you win.

You start on 20 life. In Commander you start on 40.

I keep the numbers. I do not know what your cards do. When a card and I disagree, the card is right.

title: Lands and mana
text:
Lands make mana. Mana pays for everything else.

You may play one land on each of your turns. Turn a land sideways to take its mana. That is called tapping. It turns upright again at the start of your next turn.

There are five colours. Plains make white, Islands blue, Swamps black, Mountains red, Forests green. A card's cost says how much mana it needs, and of which colours.

title: Kinds of card
text:
Creature: stays in play, attacks and blocks. Its two numbers are power and toughness.

Sorcery: happens once, on your own turn only.

Instant: happens once, at almost any time, even on someone else's turn.

Enchantment and artifact: stay in play and keep doing something.

Planeswalker: an ally with its own counters. Opponents can attack it.

For what a particular card does, read the card. Or tap Card and I will find it.

title: What the button does
text:
Press: the next step, or the next turn if you set me to whole turns.

Press twice: undo the last change. Life, poison, damage, all of it.

Hold: ask me something. Keep it simple.

The plus and minus keys change life by one. The keys marked 5 change it by five, for the larger disasters.

title: A first game
text:
Use two simple decks and play with your hands face up.

Turn one: lands and mana. Turn two: creatures, and why they cannot attack yet. Turn three: attacking and blocking.

Leave instants until somebody holds one and wants to use it.

Then play again with hands hidden. You will lose differently.

title: A turn: the beginning
text:
The button walks through the turn. The name of each step is at the top of my screen.

Untap: turn all your cards upright.

Upkeep: anything that happens at the start of your turn happens now.

Draw: take one card. With two players, whoever goes first skips this on the very first turn.

title: A turn: the middle
text:
First main: play a land, cast what you can afford.

Combat: choose attackers and tap them. The defender chooses blockers. Then damage is dealt.

Second main: another chance to play a land, if you have not, and to cast things.

title: Combat
text:
Only the attacker decides who attacks. Only the defender decides who blocks.

A creature deals damage equal to its power. If it takes damage equal to its toughness or more, it is destroyed.

An attacker nobody blocks hits the player instead. Tap that player's life down.

A creature that survives is as good as new at the end of the turn.

title: A turn: the end
text:
End step: anything that happens at the end of your turn happens now.

Cleanup: if you hold more than seven cards, discard down to seven. Damage on creatures wears off.

Then the next player begins.

title: Mistakes everyone makes
text:
A creature cannot attack on the turn it arrives. It can still block.

Attacking taps a creature, and a tapped creature cannot block. What you hold back matters.

When someone casts a spell, everyone may answer it with an instant. The last thing cast happens first.

A card that is destroyed or cancelled goes to the discard pile, not back to your hand.

title: Ways to be out
text:
Your life reaches 0.

You collect ten poison counters.

In Commander, one opponent's commander deals you 21 combat damage over the whole game.

You have to draw a card and your deck is empty. I cannot see your deck, so tap Counters, then Out, when that happens.

I warn you one step before each of the first three.

title: Commander
text:
Four players is usual. Each has a deck of exactly 100 different cards led by one legendary creature: the commander.

Your commander waits to one side until you cast it. Each time you cast it from there again, it costs 2 more.

Tap a player on my screen to record damage from a commander. I take it off their life as well, and I count each commander separately. 21 from any one of them is a knockout, whatever their life says.

title: Poison and the monarch
text:
Some cards hand out poison counters. Ten and you are out. Counters keeps the tally.

Some cards make a player the monarch. There is only ever one. The monarch draws an extra card at the end of their own turn. A creature that deals combat damage to the monarch takes the crown for its owner.

Tell me who holds the crown under Counters and I will remind them to draw.
